briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Domestic and International Climate Crisis Status and Accelerating Impacts
sections.content: The news released today clearly demonstrates the deepening global crisis caused by climate change. Domestically, climate change has accelerated the activity period of pine wilt disease vectors by two weeks, making control more difficult [1]. On the Korean Peninsula, the combined risk of heatwaves and heavy rainfall has increased, and extreme weather phenomena, such as a rain cloud front moving 213km northward, continued until September [2, 5]. Internationally, a grim report revealed that 96% of the world's coastal coral reef ecosystems are in a 'critical' state, facing a risk of complete collapse within 50 years [4]. Furthermore, the deadly heatwave that struck Europe this summer resulted in approximately 50,000 deaths, with two-thirds of these attributed to climate change [32, 34, 36, 39, 40, 42].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts and Technological Advancements for Carbon Neutrality Transition
sections.content: Amidst these crises, various efforts to transition to a carbon-neutral society are continuing both domestically and internationally. Domestically, the Korea Meteorological Administration is attempting precise climate change analysis by adding aerosols to its Chupungnyeong climate change observation items [3], and criteria for designating 'Just Transition Special Zones' to support areas affected by carbon neutrality have been established [11]. Festivals and campaigns for carbon neutrality practices and environmental education are actively underway in various local governments, including Gwacheon City and Gwangmyeong City [9, 10, 12, 14], and measures to encourage citizen participation, such as quadrupling carbon neutrality points for bicycle use, have also been introduced [8]. Internationally, a University of Minnesota researcher has created a new dissemination channel for climate change research [24], and the ABA (American Bar Association) is working to establish research and institutional foundations by publishing new practice guides on sustainable real estate development and climate change [25]. The City of Bellevue is encouraging young people to implement their climate action ideas, emphasizing the role of future generations [30].

sections.title: ⚠️ Complex Challenges in Energy Transition and Climate Policy
sections.content: The transition to carbon neutrality presents complex, non-trivial challenges. Domestically, concerns have been raised that the use of LNG (liquefied natural gas) in the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster could run counter to carbon neutrality goals [13], and critical perspectives exist regarding renewable energy subsidies [22]. Internationally, a report indicates that rising costs have weakened Californian residents' support for greenhouse gas reduction [31], suggesting that economic burdens can hinder the momentum of climate action. These challenges demonstrate the need for a nuanced approach in policy formulation and securing public support during the energy transition process.

sections.title: 🌍 Rising Importance of Climate Change Adaptation and Emergency Preparedness
sections.content: As the impacts of climate change become a reality, the importance of adaptation and emergency preparedness is growing. News that corn farmers are adapting to climate change demonstrates efforts for change in the agricultural sector [29]. The UK government is emphasizing disaster preparedness, recommending citizens to stockpile emergency supplies through its 'Be Ready' campaign [44, 45]. Meanwhile, the news that Nepal has become the first country to receive climate change reparations highlights the need for international responsibility and support for losses and damages caused by the climate crisis [41]. The fact that conversations about climate change are happening through individual contact [27] suggests the importance of shifting public awareness and communication.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, the various efforts to overcome it, and the challenges we face. Through continuous interest and cooperation, we must build a climate-resilient future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
